name: Chi-square (independence / goodness of fit)
when_to_use: Two categorical variables arranged in a contingency table; test whether they are associated (independence) or whether an observed distribution matches an expected one (goodness of fit).
notes: Checks whether two categorical variables (e.g., gender x product preference) are related or whether it is coincidence. Applications: satisfaction survey cross-tabulated with customer profile.

expected_input.question: Are two categorical variables associated, or is it coincidence?

pdca_use: Check phase: verify whether the distribution of a cause/category (e.g., type of nonconformity) changed after the action, or whether two categorical causes are associated.

plain_explanation.purpose: Checks whether two categorical variables are related or independent.
plain_explanation.when_to_use_plain: When two categories are cross-tabulated and you want to know whether the link is real.
plain_explanation.data_needed: A table of counts crossing two categorical columns.
plain_explanation.example: See whether the acquisition channel influences the type of plan chosen.
plain_explanation.diagram: observed vs. expected if there were no relationship -> large difference = relationship
